chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who owed me property, but he disputed me over it and swore an oath. Then some of his property came into my possession. Should I take it in place of my property which he took and swear over it as he did?
So he said: If he has betrayed you, then do not betray him, and do not enter into that for which you blamed him.

key_terms.خَانَكَ: he betrayed you or acted treacherously toward you
key_terms.عِبْتَهُ: you censured or blamed him for it
key_terms.فَلَا تَخُنْهُ: do not respond with betrayal in return

ai.seo_question: Can someone recover stolen or denied property by secretly taking the other person's money and swearing falsely?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a person is not permitted to respond to betrayal with betrayal, even when reclaiming what he believes is his due. It emphasizes moral restraint and condemns adopting the same wrongful conduct one criticizes in others.
